parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer (binary sex definition, no X/self-selected passport markers, visa refusal and possible lifetime fraud findings on document discrepancy, federal-facility exclusion, documented abuse in immigration custody) with a state layer in the top 'Do Not Travel' tier: birth-certificate restroom rule in all state buildings/schools/prisons, active enforcement (ID checks, first state bathroom-law investigation), an arrest and 24-hour male-ward holding, no state discrimination law, hate-crime law excluding gender identity, and a definition act barring marker changes. No criminalisation of identity, no death penalty, and some courts/aid groups push back, but hostile policy is efficiently enforced and remedies are partial.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order ended X markers and self-selection; visa officers told to refuse where document discrepancy casts doubt on sex, with lifetime fraud ineligibility considered; trans travellers report passports blocked/confiscated, some stranded abroad; multiple foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires all four elements, is never automatic, with limited waiver; litigation pending.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening feeds into state facility rules: document mismatch discovered at entry follows the traveller into every state building check.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State trespass charge (up to 60 days) for restroom use after refusal to leave; one trans woman arrested and held 24 hours in the men's ward. Federal immigration custody documents forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees; federal prisons adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (haircut, hormone removal).
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Facility offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; courts denied immunity but 2019 surgery claim failed; some orders enjoined nationally.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor stopped for document or restroom discrepancy can move from administrative check to criminal charge to birth-sex holding.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law (in force 4 Dec 2025) requires restrooms to match birth-certificate sex across schools, universities, prisons and state buildings, with $25k/$125k facility fines; nationwide, 22 state/provinces ban identity-congruent facility use, 4 criminalise it. Enforcement began within days, including police ID checks at capitol restrooms.
federal_state_facilities.protection: In 29 state/provinces plus capital district no such mapped ban; troopers admitted trans women holding female ID markers in one episode; some private settings unaffected in most units.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal and state bans stack for a visitor in any public building; unclear guidance produces uneven, invasive checks.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors (so a travelling trans minor can be refused routine care) and bars marker changes; nationally care for under-18s banned in 27 units, proposed rule bars public-insurance reimbursement; LGBTQ youth crisis services shut down.
care_services.protection: Care restrictions target minors and resident systems; adult visitor's own-country prescriptions not shown to be seized; legal-aid FAQ on documents exists.
care_services.interaction: For an adult travelling with a trans minor, minor-focused bans become directly traveller-facing at any clinic.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official framing treats trans presence as threat: tip-line-driven DOJ escalation against a school district, 'chemical and surgical mutilation' order, counterterrorism strategy naming 'radically pro-transgender' groups, cash-reward language around 'radical gender ideology'; city LGBTQ ordinance rescinded, Pride suspended.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria do not list gender ideology; counterterrorism text says it will not target mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing plus federal rhetoric raises outing probability and reduces likelihood of sympathetic police response.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling trans minors face facility bans at schools/universities, state deadnaming/misgendering mandate in schools, and denial of gender-affirming care; national order directs investigating schools and prosecuting facilitators of social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Criminal exposure directed at teachers/facilitators, not documented against visiting parents; several directives blocked or enjoined; five DAs refused to follow earlier directives.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting family entering school or clinic settings steps into resident-facing rules with investigative machinery behind them.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 44 recorded killings of trans women 2008-2025 (~7.6/100k/yr), described as national worst in absolute terms; state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity and prosecutions are rare; LGB-facing visibility rolling back.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Dossier explicitly cannot compare this rate to the state's general homicide rate, so it reads as background-level, not organised targeting; no state sodomy law nationally and same-sex conduct decriminalised in 2003.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin state bias-motivated-violence coverage means an assault on an outed visitor may go unpunished.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide discrimination law; hate-crime law excludes gender identity; enforcement guidance unclear, only two documented check episodes; school-district investigation outcome unsourced; renewal of existing changed markers after Sept 2025 act unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit over passports pending, several executive orders enjoined, cities prohibit gender-identity discrimination, legal-aid FAQ maintained, national employment and hate-crime statutes apply.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate slowly and mostly in the resident sphere, so a short-stay visitor largely faces the operative rules as enforced.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like Vellandra, exposure is administrative and universal (entry refusal, facility exclusion, humiliation) rather than custodial or lethal, and appeals are slow. Lower than 0.35-A because refusal is not near-automatic—waivers exist, courts have enjoined several orders, and identity itself is not criminalised.

Closest match: routine exposure at checks and facilities, documented detention and humiliation, prosecutions for visitors uncommon, inconsistent enforcement, narrow and slow remedies. Rated slightly below because hostile policy here is efficiently enforced (ID checks, first enforcement inquiry) and immigration-custody abuse is documented.

Higher than Kestrel Isles, where harm stays administrative (refused admission, secondary screening). Here document discrepancy can trigger fraud-referral plus a criminal trespass pathway and male-ward holding, and facility rules bind in every state building.

Well below Meridia: no trained respectful inspection, no tribunal for document-fraud detention, active marker ban, facility exclusion by birth certificate, and a state-assessed top 'Do Not Travel' tier rather than low-severity screening friction.

parsed.synthesis: Federal and state rules operate as one system. The federal document regime maximises discovery (no X marker, discrepancy-based refusal, possible fraud finding), while the state supplies a criminal-adjacent facility rule enforced with ID checks and a documented arrest ending in male-ward holding. Discovery therefore moves border → building → custody. Protections are real but partial: identity is not criminalised, some orders are enjoined, cities and legal-aid groups assist, and the violence rate cannot be shown above background. But hostile policy is efficiently enforced (liability clause applies), state bias-crime coverage excludes gender identity, and remedies are slow and largely resident-facing—leaving the outed visitor with friction, exclusion, and a credible arrest-and-holding pathway rather than imprisonment as the norm.
